keyConcept: Facial colliculus: facial nerve wraps around abducens nucleus in floor of fourth ventricle.
Cerebral aqueduct connects third ventricle to fourth ventricle.
Fourth ventricle communicates with subarachnoid space via lateral apertures of Luschka and median aperture of Magendie.
Contralateral pain and temperature loss below lesion: lateral spinothalamic tract lesion.
Face represented upside down in somatosensory cortex, with larger areas for lips and fingers.
Motor branch to mylohyoid arises from posterior division of mandibular nerve (V3).
Rubrospinal tract: main indirect pathway from cerebellum via red nucleus to spinal cord.
Pain and temperature first-order neuron: pseudounipolar cell body in trigeminal ganglion.
Primary motor cortex (area 4): execution of voluntary movement.
Spinal accessory nerve: sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.
Genu of corpus callosum supplied by anterior cerebral artery.
Lateral pterygoid muscle lies on medial surface of infratemporal fossa.
Supplementary motor area located in medial aspect of frontal lobe (medial area 6).
Brocas motor speech area in inferior frontal gyrus (dominant hemisphere).
Temporalis is the chief retractor of mandible.
Sensory dorsal horn develops from alar lamina of neural tube.
Cuneocerebellar tract carries unconscious proprioception from upper limb to cerebellum.
Tongue deviation toward lesion with ipsilateral atrophy: hypoglossal nerve lesion.
Superior cerebellar peduncle carries dentatothalamic fibers from cerebellum to thalamus.
Cavernous sinus thrombosis from facial infection: danger area around nose/upper lip.
